ai_show_review.summary: Epic Dark Star leads a fiery set with standout The Eleven
ai_show_review.blurb: The March 29‑’69 Ice Palace show is anchored by an extraordinary Dark Star that rolls into the classic Holy Trinity (Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven). Jerry’s soaring solos and Phil’s booming bass underpin a tight, high‑energy performance. The set also features a lively Doin’ That Rag and a bluesy turn with Turn On Your Lovelight.
ai_show_review.review: On March 29, 1969 the Grateful Dead took over Las Vegas’s Ice Palace for a one‑hour‑plus set that still shines for its psychedelic intensity. The centerpiece is an epic Dark Star—described across all four soundboard captures as “phenomenal” and “soaring”—that launches straight into Saint Stephen and then The Eleven, delivering the coveted ‘Holy Trinity’ sequence with relentless drive. Jerry Garcia’s guitar work is universally praised; his leads are called “hot,” “perfect,” and a highlight of the night, even if opinions on his vocals vary. Phil Lesh provides “booming bass bombs” that lock in solidly with the dual‑drum attack of Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann, while Pigpen’s bluesy presence adds extra flavor to the early numbers. The set rounds out with a raucous Doin’ That Rag and a spirited Turn On Your Lovelight, making this Ice Palace performance a must‑listen for anyone chasing ’69 psychedelia.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard capture with crystal‑clear balance, no flaws, and the definitive Dark Star performance.

band_performance.Phil: Receives praise for booming bass bombs and sounding great throughout the set.
